lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. His name is Alex and he's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! I'd like to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are specific rules that apply. For children aged 16 or over but under 20, you can still qualify for Child Benefit if they're in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, or in an approved training program)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in college studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great - being in college studying for A-levels would typically count as approved education.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit would pay towards his upkeep** (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Remember, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. One final question:

**Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started any work, and he's not receiving any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 17 and still in approved education (studying A-levels at college), which means the age requirement is met (children under 20 in approved education qualify)
- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you, so you're responsible for him
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex hasn't started full-time work (24+ hours per week) or claimed benefits in his own right

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay back some or all of it through tax.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
